summary: A paged setup in a dialog, one step at a time, with a step bar and choices to pick on the way.

props.name: triggerIcon
props.description: A glyph beside the trigger's label.

props.name: iconPosition
props.description: Which end of the trigger its `triggerIcon` sits at.

props.name: steps

example.title: Welcome to your files
example.description: Three quick steps to set up where your files live and how they sync.

example.title: Choose what to keep in sync
example.description: Pick folders now; you can change this any time in Settings.

example.title: You are all set
example.description: Your folders sync in the background. Change any of this later in Settings.

props.description: Each step's `title`, `description` and optional `choices`. Steps advance one at a time and the dialog resets to the first when it closes.

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Called on the last step's Done with the id of every picked choice.

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Esc closes the tour, as it does any dialog. Turn it off for a tour that must be finished or closed from its last step.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner radius on the trigger, the popup and its controls.

props.name: animated
props.description: The slide transition between steps and the popup's scale-in. Turn it off for an instant tour, or when the user has asked for reduced motion.

props.name: focus
props.description: The focus outline. `true` draws it, `false` removes it along with the danger, error and success tints that ride with it, and a string of Yumma CSS utilities restyles it on every focusable part of the component, which is more than `className` reaches. Removing it outright and putting nothing back fails WCAG 2.4.7.

props.name: container
props.description: Where the popup is rendered. Defaults to `document.body`, which is right almost always; pass an element to portal somewhere else, such as inside a frame or a container that owns its own stacking context.
